newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CPC sees oil pipeline ready by September 1999.
newsitem.headline: CPC sees oil pipeline ready by September 1999.

text.p: The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which signed a deal Friday to build a $2 billion oil pipeline from Kazakhstan to Russia, expects to complete the route by September 1999, a group member said at the signing.

Jeet Bindra, president of the Chevron Pipe Line Company, said the pipeline, running from Kazakhstan's huge Tengiz field to the Russian Black Sea export outlet of Novorossiisk, should be ready by then and that oil could start to flow immediately.

"I expect the pipeline to be completed by September 1999," he said after the signing ceremony. He added that the pipeline would be kept full as it progressed, and that exports could therefore start immediately.
He said the initial capacity of the pipeline would be 28 million tonnes a year (560,000 barrels per day), rising progressively to 67 million tonnes (1.34 million bpd) by 2012 to 2014.
New facilities at Novorossiisk are also to be built to handle new volumes.
"Initially we will have two single point moorings at the port, and will add more as volumes increase," he said.
Bindra said other pipelines will be needed to take Central Asian crude to world markets.
"Total oil production in the region will exceed oil pipeline capacity, including the CPC, in the future," he added.
The CPC deal allows full project financing and contruction on the project to proceed, CPC said in a statement earlier.

Chevron Corp owns 15 percent of CPC, Russia's LUKoil 12.5 percent, Mobil Corp and Russia's Rosneft 7.5 percent each, BG Plc and Italy's Agip SpA two percent each, and Oryx Energy Company and Kazakhstan's Munaigaz 1.75 percent each. The remaining 50 percent is divided between Russia (24 percent), Kazakhstan (19 percent) and Oman (seven percent).
